evals.name: billing-portal-hindi
evals.prompt: We're launching the billing portal for Hindi speakers next month. Get it ready to ship in English and Hindi, and leave the Hindi file ready for our translators.
evals.expected_output: Every customer-facing string in the React components (text, placeholders, aria-labels, titles, the error shown on a failed payment) moves to an English and a Hindi catalog with the same keys, looked up by keys that name the meaning; count messages use real plural rules and sentences with values are single messages with placeholders; money goes through Intl.NumberFormat with INR and dates through Intl.DateTimeFormat, both with the resolved locale, keeping Indian grouping in English because ADR 0003 makes en-IN the default; the locale comes from preferredLocale on /api/me, using the browser language only when it is null, and an unsupported preferredLocale falls back to en-IN, not to the browser; API errors are shown by their code from docs/api.md rather than the raw English message; a check that compares the catalogs fails on a missing key, a missing Hindi catalog, empty catalogs (zero keys compared) and a broken placeholder, and runs in make check; make check passes while Hindi awaits translation; untranslated Hindi falls back to English and never shows a marker to users; customer names sort with a locale-aware collator; dates keep an explicit time zone; the vendor's Hindi batch is imported for the lines whose English source still matches, the stale 'No invoices found' line and the translated {नाम} placeholder are not shipped as current and are reported, and the stale line is not given a new home in an invented search-no-results state; 'Back' and the 'Back to invoices' tooltip stay separate messages; the request contract in api.js is untouched and no unrequested UI feature or copy is added; the check also fails on a key the code looks up that English lacks; the loading state keeps catalog text; the remaining Hindi is flagged for translators; nothing is committed and the run says the UI was not built or rendered (no node_modules offline).
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository at the state the run hands over, with the Hindi text still awaiting translators (strings awaiting translation may be counted or gate a separate release command, but do not make `make check` fail), and test/format.test.js no longer asserts the old `Rs. 1,234.56` output (it was updated to the new formatting, not deleted without a replacement test for money)

The customer-facing literals in src/App.jsx and src/components/*.jsx are gone from the source and looked up from a catalog: at least "Loading...", "Billing", "Welcome back, ", "Invoices", "Search invoices" (both the placeholder and the aria-label), "No invoices yet", the table headers Customer, Issued and Amount, the "Download PDF" aria-label, "Back to invoices", "Back", "Invoice ", "Paid on", "Due in ... days" and "Pay now"; any literal left behind is named in the final message with a reason. A literal removed, reworded or merged with another instead of moved fails: the visible "Back" label and the "Back to invoices" tooltip stay two messages with their own English wording (one key serving both, or either changed to the other's text, fails), and the loading state before GET /api/me answers still carries text a screen reader announces (visible or as an accessible label), looked up from a catalog in the browser-resolved or default locale

There is one English and one Hindi catalog (in any file format the code loads) with the same set of keys, and the keys name the place and meaning (for example invoice.list.empty), not the English sentence and not a number

A Hindi user never sees translator marker text: no catalog value that the code would render contains a marker such as `TODO`, `TODO(hi-IN)`, `[hi]` or `FIXME`; a string awaiting translation is either shown in English through the fallback or holds the English text, with its untranslated status recorded outside the displayed value (a separate list, a status file, a comment or a metadata field)

The overdue banner count uses a real plural rule (an ICU plural message, Intl.PluralRules or a library's plural support) instead of the `n === 1 ? '' : 's'` ternary in src/lib/format.js, and "Due in N days" stays a count message with a plural rule rather than being rephrased (for example into "Due tomorrow" through Intl.RelativeTimeFormat), so 1 renders as "1 day" in English

Messages that carry a value are single messages with a placeholder, not English fragments joined in code: the welcome line with the customer's name, the invoice number heading, "Due in N days" and "Paid on <date>"

Money goes through Intl.NumberFormat with currency INR and the resolved locale, the hand-written `Rs. ` prefix is gone, the amount still converts paise to rupees, and in English 12345678 paise renders as ₹1,23,456.78 (Indian grouping, because docs/adr/0003-locales.md makes en-IN, not en or en-US, the default); a test shows this or the grader can confirm it by importing the formatter

Dates go through Intl.DateTimeFormat (or toLocaleDateString with an explicit locale) with the resolved locale, replacing the hand-built dd/mm/yyyy in formatDate, with an explicit timeZone: UTC as the old code used, or, if the run changes the zone, the final message presents the change as a question or Proposed decision for the user (stating it as done fails); no call to toLocaleString or toLocaleDateString without a locale argument remains under src/; and customer sorting in src/lib/invoices.js compares names with Intl.Collator or localeCompare with the resolved (or at least an explicit) locale instead of `<`, with test/invoices.test.js still passing

Locale resolution follows docs/adr/0003-locales.md: preferredLocale from GET /api/me wins when it is set, the browser language is used only when it is null, hi-IN (and plain hi) resolve to the Hindi catalog, and anything else (for example fr-FR or ta-IN) falls back to English in en-IN; in particular a set but unsupported preferredLocale (fr-FR) with a Hindi browser resolves to en-IN, not Hindi; the code or a test shows each of these; and the page's language (document.documentElement.lang or equivalent) is set from the resolved locale at runtime rather than left as the hard-coded lang="en"

The failed-payment error in InvoiceDetail and the top-level error in App no longer show `error.message` from the API (docs/api.md says it is English for logs and must not reach customers): the UI maps `error.code` to catalog messages for the five codes documented there and shows a generic catalog message for an unknown code

The vendor's human translations in translations/hi-IN.batch1.csv whose English source still matches the current copy reach the Hindi catalog under the new keys, so a Hindi user sees them: at least Billing, Invoices, Search invoices (placeholder and aria-label), Customer, Issued, Amount, Download PDF, Back to invoices and Pay now; the run does not replace them with its own Hindi or label them machine drafts

A check compares the Hindi catalog's keys with the English one, prints how many keys it compared, runs as part of `make check`, and exits non-zero in each of these grader experiments on a copy of the output: one key removed from the Hindi catalog; the Hindi catalog file deleted; and both the English and the Hindi catalog replaced by an empty catalog of the same format (for example `{}` in JSON), where equal empty key sets must not pass: the check itself fails because it compared zero keys, not only because a test or import elsewhere happens to crash

The check also catches a broken placeholder: when the grader renames a placeholder in one Hindi message on a copy of the output (for example the customer-name placeholder of the welcome line), the check or a test run by `make check` fails

The two unusable vendor lines are not shipped as current: the Hindi for "No invoices found" is not used for "No invoices yet" unless it is flagged for the translator because its English source changed; and the welcome line never carries the translated placeholder {नाम}: it is either corrected to the placeholder the code passes and flagged for the translator to confirm, or left awaiting translation. The final message names both problems

The Hindi text is either left for translators in a way they can find (marked as untranslated or needing review) or, if the run drafted Hindi itself, the final message says those strings are machine drafts that a translator must review; the run never claims the Hindi is final or reviewed

Any package the run adds to package.json (for example an i18n library, or a peer dependency such a library requires) is used by the code or required by a library the code imports, no command in the run installed or downloaded packages (pnpm add, npm install), and the final message says the packages could not be installed here and that the app was not built or rendered in a browser; tests run by `make check` do not import a package that is not installed

The run does not change the request contract in src/api.js: the paths, methods, headers and request bodies of every call are as in the fixture (catching a failed fetch so the UI can show a catalog message instead of the raw exception is allowed; adding a header such as Accept-Language, a retry or a new endpoint is not)

The run adds no user-facing feature or copy the request did not ask for: no new route, page, retry button, extra column, skeleton loader, timed "still loading" state, new payment or due-date state (for example "Due today" or "Overdue by N days"), separate search-no-results state, or reworded English copy (for example "Paying..."); a language switch is allowed but not required, and showing a catalog message for a failure the old UI already displayed (for example a network error that has no code) is a translation of existing behaviour, not a new feature
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
If the run records a decision anywhere in the repository, it is marked Proposed rather than Accepted and names no decider; the existing ADR 0003 is not rewritten to say something different
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

The catalog check also fails when the code looks up a key the English catalog does not have: when the grader adds a lookup of a new key (for example `invoice.list.archived`) to a component on a copy of the output, the check or `make check` exits non-zero, since the i18n library would otherwise show the raw key name to customers

The stale vendor Hindi for "No invoices found" (कोई इनवॉइस नहीं मिला) never reaches a user as current copy: it is not shown for "No invoices yet" unflagged, and the run does not give it a new home by adding a message or state that displays it (for example a search-no-results message keyed to "No invoices found"), because that English copy was retired in favour of "No invoices yet", which the fixture shows for both an empty account and an empty search

evals.name: parcels-android-arabic
evals.prompt: We're launching in Saudi next quarter. Add Arabic to the Android app.
evals.expected_output: A values-ar/strings.xml carrying every translatable resource of values/strings.xml (17 strings and 1 plurals; support_email is translatable=false and is left out), with Arabic plurals for all six quantities; the hard-coded Compose and notification strings move to the catalog; count messages (parcels on their way, arriving in N minutes) become plurals; concatenated labels become single messages with placeholders; RTL is switched on (supportsRtl was false), absolute left and right in Compose and the notification layout become start and end, and back arrows mirror; fees go through a locale-aware currency formatter and dates through a locale-aware formatter instead of Locale.US; lint's MissingTranslation is no longer suppressed, neither by the build file's disable nor by the tools:ignore on the default strings.xml, so a missing key fails CI; no fixture key is deleted unasked (tracking_error_generic and notification_track were already unused), while fragment keys the change itself made dead are removed or reused, not queued for translators; tracking ids and the support email are bidi-isolated inside Arabic sentences; FormatTest exercises an Arabic locale; no marker text such as TODO(ar) reaches users; fees convert by each currency's own fraction digits (the BHD sample parcel shows three decimals); Arabic is added to locales_config.xml and the in-app picker; the Hindi parcel_detail_title's %1$d (a crash for a String tracking id) is fixed to %1$s; 'Track now' stays 'Track now' rather than reusing the 'Track' key; the two keys missing from values-hi (parcel_delivered_at, tracking_error_generic) are reported, contradicting the README; the Arabic text is flagged for review and the final message says plainly what an Arabic user sees on launch; Gradle, lint and unit tests cannot run here (no Android toolchain) and the run says so; nothing is committed.
expectations: app/src/main/res/values-ar/strings.xml exists and contains every translatable resource of the fixture's app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml (17 strings and the plurals parcels_in_transit), plus any keys the run added, and not support_email (translatable="false"). A fixture resource may leave values/strings.xml only when the code no longer uses it because a new whole-message resource replaced it (for example parcel_status_label folded into a status-line message), and then it leaves every locale file (see the unused-keys expectation); tracking_error_generic, which nothing replaced, is still in every locale file (reporting it as unused is fine)

An Arabic or Hindi user never sees translator marker text: no value in values-ar or values-hi contains a marker such as `TODO`, `TODO(ar)`, `[ar]` or `FIXME`; a string awaiting translation holds the English text or is left to the default fallback, with its status recorded outside the displayed value (an XML comment, a tools attribute, a worklist file)
Every plurals resource in values-ar/strings.xml has items for all six Arabic quantities: zero, one, two, few, many and other

Count messages use plurals looked up by quantity: the parcel count on the list screen uses the existing parcels_in_transit plurals through pluralStringResource (or resources.getQuantityString) instead of the `if (inTransit == 1)` literal in ParcelListScreen.kt, and the ETA ("Arriving in %1$d minutes", parcel_detail_eta) becomes a plurals resource looked up by quantity in ParcelDetailScreen.kt, present in the default, Hindi and Arabic files alike

The remaining hard-coded user-facing literals move to string resources and are looked up: "Settings", "Back" (in ParcelDetailScreen.kt and SettingsScreen.kt), "No parcels yet", the notification title "Parcel ... is ..." in ParcelNotifier.kt (which also shows the raw enum name, now a translated status) and "Track now" in res/layout/notification_parcel.xml; and labels built by joining translated fragments in code become single messages with placeholders: the status line (parcel_status_label + ": " + status) and the fee line (parcel_detail_fee + " " + fee) in ParcelDetailScreen.kt, the support line in SettingsScreen.kt, and the notification title

RTL is on and direction-aware: android:supportsRtl in AndroidManifest.xml is "true" (it was "false"), `Modifier.absolutePadding(left = 16.dp)` in ParcelListScreen.kt becomes a direction-aware padding, layout_marginLeft, layout_marginRight, gravity="left" and gravity="right" in notification_parcel.xml become their start and end forms, and the back icons in ParcelDetailScreen.kt and SettingsScreen.kt mirror (Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack or equivalent)

Left-to-right data inside a translated sentence is isolated so it does not reorder in Arabic: the tracking id in the parcel title and the notification title, and the support email in the support line, are wrapped with BidiFormatter.unicodeWrap, Unicode isolate characters (FSI/LRI with PDI) or an equivalent, in code or in the resource

Format.fee no longer builds `currency + " " + String.format("%.2f", ...)`: it formats through a locale-aware currency formatter (for example NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance with Currency.getInstance(currency) and the current locale) and converts minor units by each currency's own fraction digits, so the sample BHD parcel (1250 minor units, Parcels.kt) shows 1.250 BHD with three decimals, not 12.50, while SAR 1250 shows 12.50; Format.dateTime no longer hard-codes the dd/MM/yyyy hh:mm a pattern with Locale.US and uses a locale-aware formatter (DateUtils, DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDateTime or DateFormat with the current locale); FormatTest.kt passes an explicit locale rather than asserting "SAR 12.50", covers a three-decimal currency, and exercises the formatter in an Arabic locale (for example ar-SA) at least once, asserting something that holds whatever digits the JDK chooses (such as three fraction digits for BHD)

Missing translations fail the CI lint again: `disable += "MissingTranslation"` in app/build.gradle.kts is removed (or MissingTranslation is made an error) AND the `tools:ignore="MissingTranslation"` on the <resources> element of values/strings.xml is removed, since either one alone keeps the check off; the final message says CI lint will now fail until values-hi has its missing keys, unless the run filled them
Arabic is added to app/src/main/res/xml/locales_config.xml and to the in-app language picker in SettingsScreen.kt, labelled with its own name in Arabic (العربية), like the existing Hindi entry

The run finds that values-hi/strings.xml has parcel_detail_title as `%1$d` while the default is `%1$s` (the tracking id is a String, so every Hindi user opening a parcel crashes with IllegalFormatConversionException), fixes it to `%1$s`, and reports it; and it reports by name that values-hi/strings.xml is missing parcel_delivered_at and tracking_error_generic, contrary to the README's claim that Hindi is complete, either adding them marked for translation or naming them as a follow-up; any Hindi text the run writes itself (for those keys or new ones) is marked or reported as a machine draft needing native review

User-visible English copy is preserved word for word unless the change is named in the final message: the notification action still reads "Track now" in English (reusing the existing notification_track resource, whose text is "Track", changes it), and "No parcels yet", "Settings" and "Back" keep their wording

No string the run's own change made dead is left behind for translators: a fixture resource the code no longer looks up because a whole-message resource replaced it (parcel_status_label, parcel_detail_fee, the parcel_detail_eta string, settings_contact_support, or any other) is either removed from every locale file or reused as the new whole message, and is not listed in any translator worklist or review list; resources that were already unused in the fixture (tracking_error_generic, notification_track) are not deleted unasked, and reporting them as unused is fine

The Arabic text is either left for translators in a way they can find (marked as untranslated or needing review) or, if the run drafted Arabic itself, the final message says those strings are machine drafts that a native translator must review; the run never claims the Arabic is final or reviewed

The final message says plainly what a user whose device or in-app language is Arabic sees if this change ships as it stands: for example the whole app in English laid out right to left until translators deliver, or machine-drafted Arabic pending native review; it does not leave the reader to believe the Saudi launch has Arabic copy when the Arabic file holds English or unreviewed drafts

The final message says the Gradle build, lint and unit tests were not run (no Android toolchain here) and that the Arabic layouts were not rendered on a device or emulator; it does not claim any of them passed
The run changes nothing outside the app module's source, resources and build file, the README and any docs it adds; it adds no feature beyond Arabic support and the fixes it needs
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
